about.summary: Named for France under Napoleon the Third: a steep mansard roof holds a whole extra floor.
about.compare: Steep mansard roof, dormers and iron cresting

cues.explain: A steep roof, almost a wall, with a full floor of rooms inside.
Windows stand out from the steep roof, in decorated frames.
A lacy iron railing runs along the top edge of the roof.
Carved brackets sit under the cornice, just below the roof.

plate.caption: George Pullman's house at Prairie Avenue and 18th Street, about 1900.
plate.credit: Detroit Publishing Co., Library of Congress

shows_style.note: No source read names this house's style. The photograph shows the features the field guide lists for Second Empire: a mansard roof, iron cresting and dormers, which the 1973 Landmarks study also describes as a French-style mansard crowned with ironwork.
